findings.detail: The problem repeats earlier questions M1-S08-T1, M1-S21-T1 and M2-S29-T1. An open-ended investigation finds something unexpected midway, and a fixed sequence, here a checklist, would miss it. The same reasoning leads to the answer: adaptive plans generate subtasks from what each step discovers. Asking which value would be lost is only a reframing of the same fixed-versus-adaptive choice. Two wrong options also repeat earlier ones. D (plan every subtask from the first request before any tool runs) repeats wrong option A of M1-S21-T1. C (the same steps in the same order on every request) repeats the fixed-same-order wrong options of M1-S21-T1 and M2-S29-T1.

blind_answer.reason: Adaptive investigation plans generate subtasks from what each step discovers (1.6-K3). Here, the Grep results revealed the YAML-based loading, so the agent added steps to read those files. A checklist written in advance could miss that path. C describes a property of fixed pipelines, not of adaptive plans. D describes upfront planning, which is the opposite of adaptive. B wrongly drops the cross-file integration pass.
